claims.claim: Increase your warehouse productivity by 2-3x with robots
Our productivity rates were 78 UPH and we're currently picking about 150 UPH
Pick from up to 600 containers per hour at each station
Picking productivity jumped from 149 to 533 pieces/person/hour
Increase throughput and maintain 99.9% uptime during peak seasons
No performance figure on its landing page

questions.why: Per robot, per station, per picker, or per facility. A per-person-hour figure can rise while the facility gets slower.

questions.q: Does the clock include travel, idle, charging and exceptions?
questions.why: A rate measured only while picking is not a rate you can staff to.
A peak hour, a good shift and a full quarter give very different numbers.

questions.q: On what order and SKU profile?
questions.why: Single-line orders of fast movers are the easiest case and the usual demo.

questions.q: At what robot-to-picker ratio, and how many of each?
questions.why: Rate per person and rate per robot move in opposite directions as you add robots. A vendor can improve one and quietly worsen the other.

questions.q: Is it a ceiling or an expectation?
questions.why: The words 'up to' convert a marketing number into an upper bound you may never see.
